short: Saudi Arabia has no binding AI statute. The binding layer is the Personal Data Protection Law, enforced by SDAIA, with fines of up to SAR 5 million; a draft Global AI Hub Law, on data-centre hubs, went to consultation in 2025.
title: Saudi Arabia AI Laws
subtitle: No AI act: the Personal Data Protection Law binds, enforced by SDAIA
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act; data protection law binds. Saudi Arabia has no binding AI statute. The Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) is the competent authority for the Personal Data Protection Law, which reaches any AI system processing personal data of people in the Kingdom. In April 2025 the Communications, Space and Technology Commission put a draft Global AI Hub Law to public consultation; despite its name it regulates data-centre hubs (private, extended and virtual), not AI systems, and no record of its enactment was found. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the Bureau of Experts laws database, the CST and Istitlaa.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedIn force
Personal Data Protection LawRoyal Decree M/19 of 9/2/1443H, amended by Royal Decree M/148 of 5/9/1444H; Cabinet Decision 9817/02/1443H (24 September 2021)720 days after publication (Art. 43 as amended), which this site computes as 14 September 2023; one further year to comply
Global AI Hub Law (draft)CST consultation draftConsultation 14 April to 14 May 2025Not enacted

Who regulates and enforces

  • SDAIA: competent authority for the PDPL; AI ethics and policy.
  • Communications, Space and Technology Commission (CST): drafted the Global AI Hub Law.

Scope and reach

The PDPL applies to any processing of personal data relating to individuals in the Kingdom, including processing by entities outside it of data on its residents, and excludes purely personal or family use (Art. 2(1)).

Core obligations

  • The PDPL's duties on consent, transfers, data protection officers and the rest, as its Implementing Regulations set them. No binding AI-specific duties were found.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Disclosing or publishing sensitive data to harm the data subject or for personal benefitUp to 2 years' imprisonment, a fine of up to SAR 3 million, or bothPDPL Art. 35Public Prosecution; competent court
Any other violationA warning or a fine of up to SAR 5 million, which may be doubled for a repeatPDPL Art. 36A committee appointed by the competent authority; appeal to the courts

What is coming next

  • Any enactment of the Global AI Hub Law; Istitlaa consultations are watched weekly.

Related

  • Global AI Laws: every jurisdiction compared, with the world map
  • AI Policy Ledger, the law tracker
  • AI lawsuit tracker and AI news

Sources

  • Personal Data Protection Law, Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers
  • CST publishes a public consultation for the Global AI Hub Law, CST
  • Global AI Hub Law, consultation, Istitlaa
  • Data governance knowledge centre, SDAIA

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: SDAIA's AI ethics principles and generative AI guidelines, and a reported 2026 draft Responsible AI Policy, because sdaia.gov.sa rejected this crawler's requests.
